column1: # Un-closed unknowns naming an address that a recorded closure elsewhere already carries.
# SEEDED, NOT DECIDED.
# check_stranded_unknowns says of itself: "A hit is a QUESTION, not a defect... the
# tool's output is a reading list, not a defect list." It has already been refined from
# 259 hits to 52 by two filters and a widened closed-item test, so what is left is
# reading. This file orders that reading.
#   SAME-SUBJECT       open bullet and closure share words beyond the address (>= 3).
#                      Read these first: they are where a question can actually close.
#   FIELD-VS-IDENTITY  the bullet asks about a FIELD (+0x..) the closure never mentions.
#                      The checker's own docstring keeps this class deliberately -
#                      01F82D20 alone accounts for three. Near-miss, rarely a defect.
#   WEAK-OVERLAP       one or two shared words. Could be either.
#   ADDRESS-ONLY       nothing but the address is shared - the adjacency failure that
#                      check_doc_claims has, in a different instrument.
# THE HINT IS NOT A VERDICT. Word overlap is not meaning: a question and its answer can
# be written in entirely different vocabulary, and two unrelated questions about one hot
# address can share a lot of words. Read the hit, not the hint - which is also what the
# checker's docstring says about its own citations, having found its first true positive
# through an unrelated register row.
# READ 2026-09-14 (OPUS): all 9 SAME-SUBJECT individually, all 21 WEAK-OVERLAP.
# ONE TRUE POSITIVE, and it is the shape the checker was built for:
#   referenced-code-the-list-never-had.md:113 asked "What the twelve mean in their own
#   subsystems... the purpose is not established for any of them" -- while UD-1 was struck
#   ANSWERED on 2026-09-13 ("ALL TWELVE READ"), and while SECTION 8 OF THE SAME PAGE
#   carried the reading the bullet said did not exist. The bullet also called 001DDAC0's
#   16/9 and 16/3 constants "suggestive and not a finding"; they are the aspect-fit ratios
#   and 001DDAC0 is the screen-mode aspect fit. Corrected in place, not deleted, because
#   the stale reading had been cited from here.
# THE OTHER 29 READ ARE NEAR-MISSES, and they are near-misses in one consistent way: the
# open bullet is NARROWER than the closure and survives it. AU-5 answers what writes +0x64
# on 01F82D20; three pages still ask what the object IS, what properties 11/19/20/21 hold,
# and what 01F82D18 beside it is - none of which AU-5 touches. DA-3 answers what supplies a
# Lua chunk; the binding page still asks WHICH SCRIPTS 00684D10 and 00686280 execute. AY-7
# identifies the 0215F000 directory; the VBF page asks about the three dwords BELOW it.
# A closure naming an address is not a closure of every question at that address.
# ALL 51 NOW READ (2026-09-14). The remaining two bands added one correction and one
# convention worth not 'fixing':
# COUNT DISCIPLINE, because the number moved for two different reasons and only one of
# them is progress. 52 -> 48 across this pass:
#   -1  UD-1, a real closure (below).
#   -1  rtti-vtable-object-model.md / 00385F60, closed by a PEER (commit a0449d2f,
#       interior citations for the 50-row frontier band). Not mine, and counted as
#       nobody's progress here.
#   -2  the two lua-loader rows LEFT THE LIST WITHOUT CLOSING. Correcting the bullet made
#       it name four addresses instead of one, which trips the checker's own MANY_ADDRS
#       filter ("an unknown that names more than two addresses is a LIST"). EB-1 IS STILL
#       OPEN. It is arguably no longer STRANDED - the bullet now cites DA-3 and says what
#       DA-3 does and does not answer - but a question that stops being visible to an
#       instrument has not been answered, and this file will not let that read as -2.
#   the-lua-loader-and-what-it-accepts.md EB-1 asserted "00684F60 in particular is a call
#   site no prior pass names". DA-3 names all three callers, on 2026-09-08 - four days
#   before that bullet's own last review. The CLAIM was struck and corrected; THE QUESTION
#   STANDS, because DA-3 gives the chain and mode=NULL and never says what any caller
#   passes as the buffer. A stale parenthetical inside a live question is its own shape.
#   shipped-standard-formats.md:187 reads `- [ ] ~~Which loader reads *.tga~~ - 00473E80
#   ... Left: whether the decoder honours the descriptor's origin bit. FR-3.` An unticked
#   box around struck text LOOKS like an inconsistency and is not: the strike closes the
#   half that was answered, the box stays open because work remains, and the residual is
#   named. check_stranded_unknowns' CLOSED_ITEM does not match `- [ ] ~~` (it wants ~~
#   directly after the dash, or x/~ in the box) and is RIGHT not to - the item is open.
#   Recorded so nobody 'repairs' the convention into a false closure.
# A SECOND FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS, on the ASK side, which the checker's filters do not cover:
# some hits are not questions at all. eastl:306 ("Not EASTL (one): 00783AA0 is MSVC's
# std::vector growth"), lua-loader:329 (a string-table line) and position-to-scalar:222
# ("That 02AEEA20 is always the identity" - a stated observation) are prose bullets inside
# a "what is not known" section. The section-membership rule admits them; nothing in them
# is open. Worth a filter if this is run again, and NOT worth one for a single pass.
